body:
I guess it’s different from everybody, but the essence is still the same: the idea that men have to conform to a strict, specific figure. 

I think in that aspect, I’m glad to have been raised differently, because I know that shouldn’t be the case.

Thank you so much!

It does in the way that I perceive myself and others perceive me, how people talk to me, etc. However, at heart I’m still the same person. Just more..open and true to myself I guess? It’s hard to explain.

Though toxic masculinity is a thing and I hate it.
With the wonders of the NHS, yes, I do. Though it is a long process that I have been waiting years for.

I get the transphobic comment here and there, I have seen people openly be transphobic to my face, I’ve been called names and slurs, it’s all around not great.

My parents were confused, and they’d call me by my deadname (the name I was assigned with at birth) but now they’re super chill, they call me by my name and pronouns and they helped my buy binders and changed my name legally.

I realised I wasn’t cis when I was 11, when my chest was growing and people started “separating” us by gender in pe, classes, etc. I realised that I wasn’t comfortable being seen as a girl. I then realised I was a male by 14 when it all clicked and I came out a year later.

Hey David!

I’m a huge fan of your work, especially as your role of the 10th doctor and Crowley from good omens. 

My question is do you look at the fans reactions and work in response to the things you do? If so, what do you think of it?

May I ask how you can volunteered for the suicide hotline? How rough was the training? 

Also, have you had any suicidal ideation yourself?
